selector.candidate_order: Concatenate search items in repository order, deduplicate repository/number, inspect at most first three distinct candidates. Stop enumeration once three candidates exist. Select first eligible candidate before any repair edit.
selector.contamination: Read issue body and source needed to reproduce; do not intentionally inspect linked fixing PRs, patch solutions, or issue comments before the repair trial. Public source and same-session evaluator mean this is not hidden or independent evidence; disclose accidental solution exposure and exclude affected candidate.
selector.disqualify: Security exploitation, credentials, access bypass, unavailable dependencies, indeterminate baseline exit, non-reproduction, flaky or network-dependent checks, or explicit already-known repair solution. Persist exact reason and move only to the next of the pre-enumerated candidates before selection; after target lock no replacement.
eligible: Public bug report has explicit expected behavior and a small deterministic local Python reproduction convertible to an assertion without secrets, external service, paid resource or unusual hardware.
The exact default-branch source can be acquired through an available authorized surface; repository license and relevant instructions are read.
Issue/target is not an earlier tested O unit, old Twisted10635, Boxoban/planning replay, self-created bug or known already-fixed example.
Unmodified source reproduces the stated expected-behavior failure with an actual non-timeout exit code, and at least one neighboring healthy upstream test/control passes.
selector.search_order: GitHub issue search sort=created order=asc per_page=3; at most one first-page query per listed repository in listed order; no alternate labels or date ranges.
